in_hebrew.name: באום
in_hebrew.long_meaning: The Hebrew name Baum is derived from the Hebrew root 'av' (father) and the suffix 'am' (multitude, people). It can be translated as 'father of a multitude' or 'father of many.' In the Bible, the name Baum is not found, but the root 'av' appears frequently, particularly as the name of various patriarchs and ancestors in the Old Testament.

in_greek.name: Βαούμ
in_greek.long_meaning: The Greek name Baum is not directly attested in the Bible or early Christian texts. However, it is possible that the name could have been transliterated from the Hebrew as Βαούμ (Baum), which could be derived from the Hebrew root 'av' (father) and the Greek prefix 'boas' (good). In this interpretation, the name Baum in Greek could mean 'good father.'

in_latin.name: Baumus
in_latin.long_meaning: The Latin name Baumus is not directly attested in the Bible or early Christian texts. However, it is possible that the name could be derived from the Latin word 'baulum' (calf, young animal), which is related to the Hebrew root 'av' (father). In this interpretation, the name Baumus could mean 'rich in living beings' or 'abundant in offspring.'
